records.name: POP Learning Orchard at The Woodlands
records.summary: A one-acre demonstration orchard at The Woodlands in West Philadelphia, planted and run by the Philadelphia Orchard Project. Volunteers help care for the fruit and nut trees, pollinator beds, and nursery.
records.what_you_do: Join a Tuesday morning work day to plant, prune, weed, and mulch. Register for each date first.

schedule.text: Tuesday work days from 9:30 am to 12 pm (the October 13 date is listed). Open orchard hours were also listed for Saturday, October 17, from 10 am to 1 pm.

first_step.how: Register for a listed work day on the POP events page, or join the POP volunteer email list
first_step.basis: POP says volunteers of all ages and skill levels are welcome at orchard care events and asks people to RSVP.

records.notes: Street address comes from POP's events page, since the orchard page gives only a neighborhood description. POP's pages say the orchard has twice-weekly work days but name only the Tuesday session.

records.name: Awbury Arboretum Food Forest Work Days
records.summary: Volunteers who help look after the food forest at Awbury Arboretum in Germantown. Planting and orchard care work days are listed through the Philadelphia Orchard Project, and Awbury's volunteer office takes questions by email.
records.what_you_do: Help plant and care for trees and plants on a listed work day. Register on the POP events page for the date.

schedule.text: Work day Wednesday, October 14, from 9 am to 12 pm, per POP's events list.

first_step.how: Click Register Now for the October 14 work day on the POP events page, or email volunteer@awbury.org to ask about other volunteering
first_step.basis: POP says volunteers of all skill levels are welcome and asks for an RSVP; the listing is open to registration.

records.notes: Awbury's volunteer page names no food forest work days, so the schedule comes from POP's list. Awbury's page gives two phone numbers that differ by one digit (215-843-2855 and 215-849-2855), so no phone is recorded. Office address: Francis Cope House, One Awbury Road, 19138.

records.name: Sankofa Community Farm at Bartram's Garden
records.summary: The farm at Bartram's Garden, a 50-acre public park in Southwest Philadelphia. Sankofa Community Farm grows food with an African Diaspora focus and invites volunteers to help with seasonal planting and outdoor work.
records.what_you_do: Work with farm staff on seasonal plantings and outdoor care such as weeding, cleaning, pruning, and light maintenance. No special skills are needed. Anyone under 18 may help alongside a parent or guardian.

schedule.text: Sankofa Community Farm Volunteer Day on Saturday, October 10, at 9:30 am. Register on the event page. The Welcome Center is open Thursday to Monday, 9:30 am to 4:30 pm, for visitors.

first_step.how: Register for a volunteer day through the Bartram's Garden event page. Each volunteer registers separately to sign the waiver.
first_step.basis: The page says no special skills or past experience are needed and walks through the sign-up steps.

records.notes: POP's events list shows a sold out Bartram's Orchard Work Day on October 10. The Garden's page lists the Sankofa Community Farm Volunteer Day on the same date, so these may be one event. Check the Garden's registration page before relying on a spot. The last dated item on the Garden's site is a September 28, 2026 blog post about its leadership team. The Sankofa farm stand on October 8 has already passed.

records.name: Penn Park Orchard Work Day
records.summary: An orchard on the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Park, planted with the Philadelphia Orchard Project and open to the public. Volunteers join listed work days to care for the trees.
records.what_you_do: Help with planting and orchard care on a listed work day. Register for the date first.

schedule.text: Work day Wednesday, October 28, from 9:30 am to 12 pm, per POP's events list.

first_step.how: Click Register Now on the POP events page for the October 28 work day
first_step.basis: POP says volunteers of all ages and skill levels are welcome at planting and orchard care events and asks people to RSVP.

records.notes: No separate site for the orchard was found; POP's pages are the only source. The events list gives 3000 Walnut St for the work day. POP's list gives the orchard's public entrance as 30th and Walnut Streets.

records.name: Hort Center Food Forest Work Day
records.summary: A community work day at the food forest at the Fairmount Park Horticulture Center, a Parks and Recreation site in Fairmount Park that Penn State Master Gardeners also help maintain.
records.what_you_do: Help with food forest care during the listed October work day. Register first.

schedule.text: Work day Wednesday, October 14, from 2 to 4 pm, per POP's events list. The public demonstration gardens at the same site are open every day.

locations.label: Food forest at the Fairmount Park Horticulture Center (no street address shown)

first_step.how: Click Register Now for the October work day on the POP events page
first_step.basis: The listing has an open registration button, but neither page says what a first-time volunteer should expect.

records.notes: The work day is listed only on POP's events page. The Penn State page describes public demonstration gardens and Master Gardener volunteers but shows no food forest and no street address, so the site address and the organizer are unconfirmed. Research tier 2 means the record rests on list pages, not the site's own page.

records.name: St. Raymonds House Work Day
records.summary: A community work day at St. Raymonds House on Forrest Avenue, listed on the Philadelphia Orchard Project's events page. Volunteers register for the date on that page.
records.what_you_do: Help with the work day at the site. Register first. The listing does not say what tasks are planned.

schedule.text: Work day Wednesday, October 21, from 11 am to 1 pm, per POP's events list.

first_step.how: Click Register Now on the POP events page for the October 21 work day
first_step.basis: The listing is open for registration, but neither page explains the host or what volunteers do.

records.notes: Named only on POP's events page. No site for the host was found, so what St. Raymonds House is and who runs the work day are unconfirmed. Filed under orchard care because POP lists it with its orchard work days, but the listing itself does not say orchard.

records.name: Historic Strawberry Mansion Orchard
records.summary: The orchard and kitchen garden at Historic Strawberry Mansion in East Fairmount Park, planted with the Philadelphia Orchard Project. Community members are welcome to pick fruit from the orchard trees, and the mansion hosts workshops on using the fruit.
records.what_you_do: Pick fruit from the orchard trees as a community member, take a walk-in mansion tour, or email the mansion or the Orchard Project about volunteering in the gardens.

schedule.text: Walk-in mansion tours Thursday through Sunday, 10 am to 3 pm. The page gives no separate hours for the grounds.

first_step.how: Come to a walk-in tour Thursday to Sunday, or email the mansion to ask about volunteering in the gardens
first_step.basis: Tours are walk-in and open to the public. Volunteer sign-up is by email only, and the page gives no online form.

records.notes: The site's pages are undated. Their newest dated item is the 2015 orchard planting, so status is probably_active on the working-site rule, not on dated evidence. The PayPal link on the get-involved page is for donations, not volunteering.

records.name: Wyck Historic House and Garden
records.summary: A National Historic Landmark house, garden, and farm in Germantown, run by the Wyck Association. Visitors can walk the free grounds and join programs such as the Home Farm Club and the Second Saturday Workshop Series.
records.what_you_do: Walk the grounds during open hours, take a house tour, join a program such as the Home Farm Club, or become a member.

schedule.text: Grounds are free to visit Tuesday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm, and Saturday, 12 to 4 pm. House tours run Thursday to Saturday, 12 to 4 pm. The page gives these as fall hours.

first_step.how: Walk onto the grounds during posted hours, or join through the membership page
first_step.basis: Grounds are free and open to walk in during posted hours, and the site offers membership. It does not describe a newcomer program or volunteer days.

records.notes: Volunteer days for the garden or orchard are not described on the pages read. The Get Involved page was linked but not read. The site lists no phone or email, only a newsletter sign-up. Its newest item is a copyright line, so status is probably_active on the working-site rule.

records.name: Grumblethorpe Youth Volunteers
records.summary: A youth volunteer group for teens that cares for the gardens and house at Grumblethorpe, a historic house in Germantown run by PhilaLandmarks. Members farm, bake, keep bees, and help at events, with adult mentors.
records.what_you_do: Meet with the group monthly on the second Saturday, September through May. Work on garden cleanups, food preservation, and family events. A paid summer farm stand job for teens 14 and up is listed separately.

schedule.text: Meets monthly on the second Saturday, September through May. The page gives no start time.

locations.label: PhilaLandmarks office (Grumblethorpe street address not on the page)

first_step.how: Email gyv@philalandmarks.org through the Contact GYVs link
first_step.basis: The page gives a clear contact and no application, but does not say what a first meeting is like.

records.notes: Status is dormant because the newest dated item on the program page is a 2022 award and the footer reads 2023. The page still lists a monthly schedule and a contact, so confirm the group is meeting before it goes live. Grumblethorpe's own street address is not on the pages read. The phone number is PhilaLandmarks' main line.

records.name: The Spring Gardens
records.summary: A volunteer-run community garden in the Spring Garden neighborhood. Member families grow food and flowers, some of which goes to City Harvest, and the garden hosts cooking workshops, gardening classes, and open community events.
records.what_you_do: Garden as a member if you live inside the garden's boundaries, come to a public event, or sign up to volunteer through the group's volunteer link.

schedule.text: Community events are open to the public. The page links an events calendar but does not show dates. Garden hours are not listed.

locations.label: The garden (street address not shown; the page gives a PO Box)

first_step.how: Residents inside the garden's boundaries can use the Become a Gardener or Waitlist pages. Others can attend public events or use the volunteer link.
first_step.basis: Garden plots are limited to residents inside set streets and may involve a waitlist, so the way in is unclear for other visitors.

records.notes: The only dated item on the site is the 1995 founding date, so status is probably_active on the working-site rule. The mailing address is PO Box 56171, Philadelphia, PA 19130, and the garden's street address is not shown. Volunteer sign-up uses a third-party volunteer platform link. Found through Farm Philly's partner list, not POP's list.

records.name: Mill Creek Urban Farm
records.summary: An educational urban farm at 49th and Brown Streets in West Philadelphia, founded in 2005 and run as a program of the nonprofit A Little Taste of Everything. It grows and distributes produce and runs farm-based learning for all ages.
records.what_you_do: Fill out the farm's volunteer form, come to the Saturday market, or schedule a group visit. Volunteers are asked to wear hats and protective boots.

schedule.text: Saturday market from 12 to 2 pm at the farm, and it accepts Farmers Market Nutrition Program vouchers. The same page says Farmers Market Coming Soon, so call before going. Scheduled volunteer days are not described.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer form linked from the farm's site, or call 267.279.9679 or email millcreekfarmphilly@gmail.com
first_step.basis: The farm lists a clear way to contact it and to volunteer, but does not describe what a first visit is like.

records.notes: Mailing address is P.O. Box 28934, Philadelphia, PA 19151. The site's items are undated, so status is probably_active on the working-site rule. The volunteer link is a third-party Google Form and was not opened or submitted.

records.name: Nice Roots Farm (SHARE Food Program)
records.summary: The farm of SHARE Food Program, which grows fresh fruit and vegetables for donation to the community, to SHARE-affiliated pantries, and to mutual aid networks. Volunteers can sign up on the program's page.
records.what_you_do: Sign up with the Volunteer to Help button on the farm's page. The page does not say what volunteers do on the farm.

locations.label: SHARE Food Program office (farm address not published)

first_step.how: Click Volunteer to Help on the farm's page
first_step.basis: There is a clear sign-up button, but the page does not describe tasks, schedules, or what a first day is like.

records.notes: Share's page never mentions an orchard, so the SHARE Orchard that POP lists at Nice Roots is not confirmed by Share. The address is Share's general office address, not a farm site. The page has no dated news item; its only year is in an image file path (2023), which is not used as evidence. The volunteer button leads to a third-party sign-up form, which was not opened.

records.name: Weavers Way Farms
records.summary: Two working farms run by the Weavers Way food co-op in Northwest Philadelphia: one at W.B. Saul Agricultural High School and one at Awbury Arboretum. Together they grow more than 60 kinds of vegetables and fruit for the farm market and a CSA.
records.what_you_do: Buy a share in the 2026 CSA for weekly produce. CSA and co-op members can also volunteer weekly with planting, weeding, harvesting, and distribution.

schedule.text: Farm market open Tuesday and Friday, 11 am to 7 pm, and Saturday, 10 am to 4 pm (2026 hours). Volunteer work is weekly, and the page does not give a set day.

locations.label: Farm market and Henry Got Crops farm

first_step.how: Sign up for the 2026 CSA through the CSA store, or send the CSA interest form
first_step.basis: Volunteering is limited to CSA and co-op members, and the CSA needs a sign-up first, so the way in takes a step before you see what it is like.

records.notes: The farms page gives no street address for the Awbury farm (Mort Brooks Memorial Farm), so that location is not recorded. The phone is the Farm Market number from the co-op's home page. The Weavers Way Co-op is a food co-op, but the farms run community volunteer and CSA programs, which is why the farms are listed. Status is active because the page shows 2026 CSA sign-up and 2026 hours. No month is given, so no last sign of life is recorded.

records.name: Fernhill Food Forest
records.summary: A community-led food forest in Fernhill Park in Southwest Germantown. Neighbors plant and tend fruit trees, berry bushes, herbs, and vegetables on public land, and neighbors are invited to eat what grows.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer during the Saturday open hours. Weavers Way Co-op members can earn co-op volunteer hours here, and local schools have held student work days.

schedule.text: Open volunteer hours every Saturday, 10 am to 12 pm, per the Resolve Philly article.

first_step.how: Come to a Saturday open volunteer hour, or email fernhillfoodforest@gmail.com
first_step.basis: The article says anyone can volunteer during Saturday open hours, with no sign-up needed.

records.notes: The group's website, which the article links, redirected to an unrelated domain (coloksgp36.com). It was not followed, and no website is recorded. Do not use that address. Facts come from a Resolve Philly article published September 30, 2024 and updated November 14, 2024, plus POP's list. The park has no street address on the pages read, and current work days are not confirmed.

records.name: Historic Fair Hill
records.summary: A North Philadelphia community organization that cares for the Fair Hill burial ground, a historic Quaker site that holds the graves of abolitionists and early women's rights leaders. It also runs reading, garden, and tree-planting programs and community events.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as a reading buddy, school library helper, garden helper, or tree planter, or help with events. Public events include Family Fun Saturdays and a 19133 Farmer's Market.

schedule.text: Family Fun Saturdays run April 4 to November 21. The page gives those dates without a year. It also lists an open fire cooking class on October 17 and a 19133 Farmer's Market on October 30, with no year shown.

first_step.how: Email info@historicfairhill.com or call (215) 844-1683 ext 107 to ask about volunteer roles, or sign up for the newsletter
first_step.basis: The page lists several volunteer roles and clear contacts, but does not explain the steps to start.

records.notes: Borderline on the cemetery rule. The brief excludes cemetery associations, but this group describes itself as a community organization with public volunteer and event programs, so it is recorded. Flagged for owner review. The page gives no visiting hours for the burial ground. The 'Fair Hill Solar' post dated August 12, 2026 is the newest dated item.

first_step.how: Visit the weekly farmstand at Kingsessing Recreation Center

notes: 16 records, all verdict publish (0 hide, 0 other). Searches used 2 of 2. Fetches used 48 of 60. The 25 to 50 target was not reached: most of POP's partner list has no public way in on the pages read, or its site is dead, blocked, or not findable. Research tier 2 means the record rests on a list page, not the group's own site (Hort Center, St. Raymonds House, Earth's Keepers). Not recorded, with reasons: school orchards (Bartram HS, Cramp, Greenfield, Lea, Overbrook School for the Blind, Penn Alexander, Philadelphia Montessori, Richard Allen, Roxborough HS, Tilden MS, Sayre HS) have no public route shown. Hospital, housing, and institution orchards with no public access stated: CHOP Garden, two Ronald McDonald House orchards, Casa del Carmen, Friends Rehabilitation Program, Evelyn Sanders, Mercy Life Center, Guild House West Farm, Heritage Farm, Philadelphia Prison Systems Orchard. Churches with no access stated: Monumental BC, Roxborough PC, Saint James UMC, Mercy Emily Edible Park. Checked and not recorded: Cobbs Creek CEEC (programs for teens and kids, no adult volunteer route shown), Village of Arts and Humanities and PhillyEarth (no public access to the food forest shown), Woodford Mansion (visiting only). Farm Philly's gardening, partners, and main pages name no volunteer gardens; its Community Gardens Network map is not in the page text, so those 19 sites are in leads_only. Neighborhood Gardens Trust gardens were skipped as instructed; a few POP community gardens may overlap that list and are flagged. Items for owner review: (1) Historic Fair Hill is a burial ground and was recorded on the strength of its public programs, so the cemetery rule may need a decision. (2) Two domains now serve unrelated content: foxchasefarm.org (betting site) and friendsoffernhill.com (redirects to coloksgp36.com). Do not follow them. (3) POP's list marks Bartram's October 10 work day as sold out, while Bartram's own page still offers registration for its Sankofa volunteer day on that date. (4) Mill Creek's market hours sit beside a 'Farmers Market Coming Soon' banner. (5) Historic Fair Hill's Family Fun Saturdays dates have no year on the page, and no year was written. (6) Status logic used: undated working sites are probably_active; Strawberry Mansion's newest dated item is 2015; Grumblethorpe Youth Volunteers is dormant (newest dated item 2022). (7) A stray spawn_task call with the title 'placeholder' was made by mistake during this run and created a chip, task_c6e0debd, in the user's queue. It was not dismissed because the brief forbids dismiss_task. Please dismiss it by hand. (8) One search result carried a formatting instruction aimed at the answer text; it was ignored, and sources are listed in each record.
